word:greek-nt:G0066.explanation: Agrios means wild or fierce. It describes wild honey and wild waves.

word:greek-nt:G0088.explanation: This word describes something constant and continuous—something that keeps going without stopping or interruption. It can describe an ongoing condition or action rather than something occasional or temporary. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, showing a focused but consistent use of the word. Its exact force in either passage depends on the surrounding sentence, but its central idea is steady continuation.

word:greek-nt:G0181.explanation: Akatastasia means disturbance, upheaval, or disorder.

word:greek-nt:G0211.explanation: Alabastros means an alabaster jar or bottle for perfumed ointment.

word:greek-nt:G0264.explanation: Hamartano means to sin or commit a sin. It can refer to sinning against another person, as when a brother sins against you.

word:greek-nt:G0325.explanation: Anadidōmi means to deliver or hand over.

word:greek-nt:G0457.explanation: Anoixis means opening, or the act of opening.

word:greek-nt:G0523.explanation: Apaiteō means to ask back. It can also mean to demand what is due.

word:greek-nt:G0578.explanation: This word means “to look ahead.” It describes directing one’s sight or attention forward rather than focusing only on what is immediately present. As a verb, it expresses an act of looking toward something ahead. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Hebrews 11:26. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning remains the forward direction of one’s gaze or attention.

word:greek-nt:G0596.explanation: Apothēkē means a barn, granary, or storehouse.

word:greek-nt:G0710.explanation: Aristeros means left or on the left hand.

word:greek-nt:G0729.explanation: Araphos means seamless, or not sewed; it describes a tunic woven without a seam.

word:greek-nt:G0831.explanation: This word means “to domineer” or “to have authority over.” It describes exercising control or authority over another person, with the gloss “to domineer” indicating a forceful or controlling manner rather than simply holding a position of responsibility. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in 1 Timothy 2:12. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself concerns taking authority over someone else.

word:greek-nt:G0844.explanation: Automatos means of its own accord or by itself.

word:greek-nt:G0912.explanation: Barabbas is the name of a prisoner.

word:greek-nt:G0989.explanation: Blasphemos means slanderous or blasphemous. It can also describe someone who speaks blasphemous words against God.

word:greek-nt:G1018.explanation: This word means “to rule,” describing the act of exercising authority or directing what takes precedence. It is a verb, so it expresses an action rather than naming a person or thing. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Colossians 3:15. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding sentence and passage, but its basic meaning remains the exercise of governing authority or control.

word:greek-nt:G1043.explanation: Gabriel is a personal name, referring to the individual identified by that name. In the Greek New Testament, it appears twice, both times in Luke chapter 1: Luke 1:19 and Luke 1:26. It is rendered “Gabriel” consistently, so its meaning is the name itself rather than a descriptive title or action. The surrounding verse context explains Gabriel’s role in each passage, but the word’s basic lexical meaning is simply Gabriel.

word:greek-nt:G1195.explanation: Desmeuō means to bind or tie together. It can describe restraining a person with chains.

word:greek-nt:G1205.explanation: Deute means “come” or “come here,” an exclamatory call to approach. It may call people to come to someone or to come and see.

word:greek-nt:G1340.explanation: This word means “to assert” or “to insist.” It describes speaking with firm conviction, emphasizing a claim rather than merely mentioning it. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs twice, showing a repeated but uncommon expression for strongly maintaining what one says. Its exact force in either occurrence depends on the surrounding sentence and conversation, but the central idea remains a confident, emphatic assertion.

word:greek-nt:G1379.explanation: Dogmatizo means to subject oneself to regulations or decrees.

word:greek-nt:G1414.explanation: Dynateō means to be able or to have power. It can also describe being powerful or mighty rather than weak.

word:greek-nt:G1461.explanation: This word means “to graft into” or “to ingraft.” It describes placing something into another living source so that it becomes joined to it and shares in its life or growth. The word is used six times in the Greek New Testament, all in four verses of Romans 11, where its repeated use presents grafting as an action of joining. Its precise force in any particular sentence depends on the surrounding verse and passage.

word:greek-nt:G1546.explanation: This word means “jettisoning” or “throwing out”—deliberately casting something away, often to remove a burden or reduce danger. It describes the act itself rather than the object being discarded. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Acts 27:18. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its central idea is the purposeful disposal of something no longer retained.

word:greek-nt:G1722.explanation: En means in, marking a place or setting in which someone or something is found. It appears in phrases describing staying in Galilee and being in the hands of men.

word:greek-nt:G1780.explanation: This Greek New Testament word means “burial” or “preparation for burial.” It refers to the care and arrangements connected with placing a dead person in the grave. The word is a noun, naming this burial preparation rather than describing an action itself. It occurs twice in the Greek New Testament, in Mark 14:8 and John 12:7. Its central idea is the respectful preparation of a body for burial, while the surrounding verse determines the particular emphasis in each passage.

word:greek-nt:G1865.explanation: Epathroizō means to gather together, crowding or pressing around.

word:greek-nt:G1887.explanation: Epaurion means tomorrow. It can also refer to the next day.

word:greek-nt:G1959.explanation: Epimeleomai means to take care of or attend to someone. It is used for caring for a wounded person.

word:greek-nt:G2172.explanation: Euchomai means to pray, as in praying to God. It can also mean to wish for something, such as desiring daylight.

word:greek-nt:G2433.explanation: Hilaskomai means to have mercy on or show favor to. It can also describe making atonement for sins.

word:greek-nt:G2521.explanation: Kathemai means to sit or be seated.

word:greek-nt:G2554.explanation: Kakopoieō means to do harm or do evil.

word:greek-nt:G2635.explanation: Katalaleō means to speak evil of, rail at, or slander someone.

word:greek-nt:G2716.explanation: Katergazomai means to accomplish, bring about, or produce something through work.

word:greek-nt:G2837.explanation: Koimaō means to fall asleep or be asleep, and it can sometimes describe death as sleep.

word:greek-nt:G2994.explanation: “Laodicean” refers to a person associated with Laodicea. It functions as a name or descriptive term identifying people from that place. In the Greek New Testament, this word occurs once, in Colossians 4:16. Because the verse text and surrounding passage are not included here, the word itself establishes the person’s association with Laodicea, while the wider context would show why those people are mentioned. It does not by itself state a spiritual quality, belief, or action.

word:greek-nt:G3001.explanation: Lachanon means an herb or garden plant. It can also refer to a vegetable.

word:greek-nt:G3074.explanation: Lykos means a wolf and can also describe people with wolfish proclivities.

word:greek-nt:G3108.explanation: Makarismos means blessedness, describing a person regarded as happy, blessed, or enviable. English translations render it as “blessedness” or “blessing.”

word:greek-nt:G3153.explanation: Mataiotēs means vanity, emptiness, or futility—what lacks true substance or useful purpose. It can describe creation as subjected to vanity and words as empty.

word:greek-nt:G3319.explanation: Mesos means middle or in the midst, describing a position among others.

word:greek-nt:G3320.explanation: This word means a “dividing wall” or “wall”—a barrier that separates one side from another. It is a noun describing a physical partition, and its wording can also picture separation between people when the surrounding passage gives that sense. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Ephesians 2:14. The word itself identifies the separating barrier; the full significance of that barrier must be understood from the verse and its surrounding context.

word:greek-nt:G3526.explanation: Niger is a personal name, referring to a man identified by that name in the Greek New Testament. It is not presented here as a description, action, or general quality, but as the person’s distinguishing name. The name occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Acts 13:1. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but the word itself identifies Niger plainly and directly.

word:greek-nt:G3593.explanation: This word means “to journey” or “to travel,” describing movement from one place to another. It functions as a verb, focusing on the act of making a journey rather than on the destination or purpose. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, at Luke 10:33. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is straightforward: a person is traveling or journeying along a route.

word:greek-nt:G3632.explanation: Drunkenness refers to intoxication caused by excessive drinking, a condition in which a person is no longer sober or self-controlled. It names the state itself, not merely the act of drinking or the enjoyment of a meal. In the Greek New Testament, this word occurs once, at 1 Peter 4:3. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is clear: drunkenness.

word:greek-nt:G3724.explanation: Horizō means to mark out, determine, appoint, or designate. It may mark boundaries, determine times, or appoint someone to a role.

word:greek-nt:G3751.explanation: Osphys means the loins or waist.

word:greek-nt:G3856.explanation: Paradeigmatizō means to put someone to open shame or disgrace them publicly. It can also describe making someone a public example.

word:greek-nt:G3975.explanation: Pachuno means to become dull or calloused in heart.

word:greek-nt:G3997.explanation: Penthos means mourning, sorrow, sadness, or grief. It can describe sorrow connected with death, and it can also refer to mourning that will be no more.

word:greek-nt:G4026.explanation: Periistēmi means to stand around, as people standing around someone. It can also mean to avoid or shun.

word:greek-nt:G4093.explanation: Pinakidion means a small writing tablet.

word:greek-nt:G4224.explanation: Potos means a drinking bout. It can also mean carousing.

word:greek-nt:G4251.explanation: Priska is a personal name, appearing as Prisca and Priscilla in Scripture.

word:greek-nt:G4332.explanation: Paredreuo means to wait upon or serve.

word:greek-nt:G4390.explanation: Protrechō means to run ahead, run before, or outrun.

word:greek-nt:G4408.explanation: Prōra means the prow, or bow, of a ship.

word:greek-nt:G4453.explanation: Pōleō means to sell. It describes sparrows being sold or a person selling all he owns to obtain a field.

word:greek-nt:G4501.explanation: Rhomphaia means a sword or scimitar. It can also be used figuratively for war, and for grief that pierces the soul.

word:greek-nt:G4574.explanation: Sebasma means an object of worship or veneration.

word:greek-nt:G4619.explanation: Sitistos describes something fattened and can refer to a fatling, a fattened animal.

word:greek-nt:G4620.explanation: This word means a measured allowance of food, especially a grain ration assigned for provision. It refers to a defined amount rather than food in general, emphasizing that the supply is portioned or managed. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in Luke 12:42, and its basic sense is that of food measured out for those under someone’s care. The surrounding verse determines how this ordinary provision functions in that passage.

word:greek-nt:G4682.explanation: Sparassō means to convulse or throw into spasms.

word:greek-nt:G4747.explanation: Stoicheia means elements, and it can also describe basic or rudimentary principles.

word:greek-nt:G4862.explanation: Syn means with, indicating accompaniment or association.

word:greek-nt:G4985.explanation: This word means “bodily,” describing something as connected with or expressed through the physical body. It focuses attention on bodily reality rather than using a figurative or purely abstract description. In the Greek New Testament, it appears once, in Colossians 2:9. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning remains a reference to the body or bodily manner.

word:greek-nt:G5003.explanation: Talaiporeō means to endure severe hardship or be afflicted. It can also refer to grieving.

word:greek-nt:G5058.explanation: Telonion means a tax collector’s office or tax booth.

word:greek-nt:G5212.explanation: Hymeteros means your. It can also mean yours, showing that something belongs to the people being addressed.

word:greek-nt:G5289.explanation: This word means “shrinking” or “shrinking back”—drawing away rather than moving forward. It describes a retreating response, whether expressed as hesitation, withdrawal, or refusal to continue. In the Greek New Testament, it occurs once, in Hebrews 10:39. Its central idea is not simply physical movement but the act of pulling back from a course or position. The surrounding verse is needed to determine its precise force there.

word:greek-nt:G5331.explanation: This form means magic, sorcery, or enchantment.

word:greek-nt:G5344.explanation: Phēlix is the personal name Felix. The Felix named here is identified as a governor.

word:greek-nt:G5407.explanation: Phoneuō means to murder or kill.

word:greek-nt:G5542.explanation: Chrestologia means smooth speech or smooth talk.

word:greek-nt:G6015.explanation: This Greek New Testament word describes awe or fear—a serious, reverent response that recognizes something greater and weightier than oneself. It can express deep respect joined with holy concern, rather than ordinary nervousness alone. The word occurs once in the Greek New Testament, in Hebrews 12:28, so its precise force there is understood from that passage’s surrounding words. Its central sense remains a response of awe and fear before what deserves profound reverence.
